caption: The magneto-optical trap at the heart of a neutral-atom system — the glowing cloud visible through the glass cell is a sample of real trapped atoms, cooled and held by laser light before individual atoms are picked out by tweezers.

steps.label: Rubidium or Cesium
steps.sub: Tightly focused laser beams hold single neutral atoms in place

steps.label: No net charge
steps.sub: Avoids the stray-field sensitivity that affects charged ions

steps.label: Reconfigurable geometry
steps.sub: Tweezers can be moved mid-computation — 1D, 2D, even 3D patterns

steps.label: Rydberg state
steps.sub: One electron promoted to a very high level — the atom balloons in effective size

steps.label: Rydberg blockade
steps.sub: A nearby excited atom blocks a second nearby atom from the same state

steps.label: That's the entangling gate
steps.sub: Briefly drive toward Rydberg, let the blockade act, return to the stable encoding

subtitle: The biggest raw qubit counts in the industry — and what that number doesn't tell you.
